findingClass: A multi-member exchange zip (NSE/BSE offer-document archive) produced a document row for only one of its members: every other non-GID member (a corrigendum, a price-band notice, an addendum) was dropped by the unwrap, so OD-30 precedence can never apply to it (F-154, failure class container-unwrapped-to-one-member).
failThreshold: For every documents row whose url is an exchange .zip and whose zip, re-read by its central directory (HTTP Range request, no full download), holds N PDF members: FAIL when the rows written from that zip (the zip url plus its '#part=<n>' member urls) number fewer than N minus the GID members minus the members the runner logged as zip_member_skipped (unclassified / too_small / too_large / same_type_as_main). Reported per IPO by name and slug with each missing member's name and position, never as a bare count (signal-ownership.md R1).
unverifiableWhen: The zip URL no longer answers a Range request (the exchange removed or moved it), or the documents row predates the item 22 zip-member change and the runner has not re-fetched that zip since.
note: zip_member_rows: SPEC ONLY - not implemented in scripts/audit-detection-floor.mjs, so it stays in notCoveredByThisManifest (counting it would read as wider coverage than the floor has; scripts/tests/audit-detection-floor.test.mjs case 79). Why not implemented here: the check needs the zip's member list, which lives only in the archive on the exchange's host; the nightly floor is a database read, and adding network reads of 41+ exchange archives to it, merged without a real-data run against staging, is the exact failure the defect-fix contract names. What guards the class today: the CI unit test scraper/tests/unit/services/zip-member-documents.test.ts drives the real runner over a zip built from real F-154 member names and asserts the exact rows written (count, type, part_number, GID writes nothing), and fails when the one-member unwrap is restored (mutation run in the item 22 zip-members PR).
owner: UNASSIGNED - owed to item 22.
